title: HelperSSHOpenChannelParams
description: One PROXIED CHANNEL to open on a pooled connection: the destination resolved by the coordinator, the kind of channel, and the caller's answer to whether a host key it has never seen may be recorded. It is a separate op from `probe` because the two differ in what they leave behind — a probe holds nothing, a channel is held until its caller closes it — and no flag can make one op mean both. Host, port and user are RESOLVED values, exactly as in probe.params: alias resolution, ~/.ssh/config merging and the credential's authorization against an endpoint stay in the coordinator.

destination.description: What to connect to and what to authenticate as.

kind.description: Which channel to open. A KIND and not a command: the helper refuses a free-form argv (host.Register refuses a bare []string), so a caller that wants a new channel adds a member to this closed set in a generation, with a protocol bump.

acceptOnTrust.description: The coordinator's answer to 'may a host key this host has never presented be recorded', carried here for the same reason probe carries it: the helper may not decide that for itself, and the decision travels with the call that started the handshake. A `changed` verdict never reaches the write whatever this says.
